claims.claim: Microsoft’s business model is built on developing and supporting a broad portfolio of technology solutions for individuals and businesses, emphasizing secure, trusted and innovative platforms across AI, cloud, productivity and personal computing.
claims.quote: We develop and support a broad portfolio of technology solutions for individuals and businesses, focusing on secure, trusted, and innovative platforms and applications that meet evolving customer needs across AI, cloud computing, productivity and collaboration, and personal computing.

claims.claim: The company offers a comprehensive set of cloud‑based services that combine AI, software, platforms and content, supplemented by solution support and consulting.
claims.quote: We offer an array of services, including cloud-based solutions that provide customers with AI, software, services, platforms, and content, and we provide solution support and consulting services.

claims.claim: Microsoft’s cloud business leverages three economies of scale—lower per‑unit compute costs, demand‑pattern aggregation, and multi‑tenant locations that reduce application‑maintenance labour.
claims.quote: Our cloud business benefits from three economies of scale: datacenters that deploy computational resources at significantly lower cost per unit than smaller ones; datacenters that coordinate and aggregate diverse customer, geographic, and application demand patterns, improving the utilization of computing, storage, and network resources; and multi‑tenancy locations that lower application maintenance labor costs.

claims.claim: Competitive positioning is reinforced by delivering secure, integrated, industry‑specific productivity and collaboration tools that work across on‑premise and cloud environments.
claims.quote: We compete by providing secure, integrated industry‑specific, and easy‑to‑use productivity and collaboration tools and services that create comprehensive solutions and work well with technologies our customers already have both on‑premises or in the cloud.

claims.claim: Azure’s competitive edge stems from its hybrid‑cloud capabilities, large‑scale infrastructure and ability to serve businesses of any size.
claims.quote: Azure’s competitive advantage includes enabling a hybrid cloud, allowing deployment of existing datacenters with our public cloud into a single, cohesive infrastructure, and the ability to run at a scale that meets the needs of businesses of all sizes and complexities.

claims.claim: The company views AI‑driven productivity as a catalyst, investing heavily in solutions such as Microsoft 365 Copilot and frontier‑AI services to expand usage and generate new revenue streams.
claims.quote: Applying AI and ambient intelligence to drive insights, revolutionize many types of work and business processes, and provide substantive productivity gains using Microsoft 365 Copilot and agents.

claims.claim: Future growth is tied to transcending traditional product categories and business models, allowing Microsoft to capture new market opportunities.
claims.quote: Our future growth depends on our ability to transcend current product category definitions, business models, and sales motions.

claims.claim: In the most recent quarter, Microsoft Cloud revenue rose roughly thirty percent year‑over‑year, underscoring accelerating adoption of cloud services.
claims.quote: Microsoft Cloud revenue was $63.9 billion and increased 30% (up 31% in constant currency) year‑over‑year.

claims.claim: Azure revenue grew by nearly fifty percent in the quarter, reflecting strong demand for infrastructure‑as‑a‑service and platform‑as‑a‑service offerings.
Commercial remaining performance obligations expanded dramatically, indicating robust future subscription and services revenue.
claims.quote: Commercial remaining performance obligation increased 73% to $677 billion

claims.claim: Microsoft completed the acquisition of Activision Blizzard in October 2023, expanding its gaming portfolio and subscription‑based services.
claims.quote: For example, in October 2023 we completed our acquisition of Activision Blizzard, Inc.

claims.claim: A long‑term strategic partnership with OpenAI is highlighted as a key element of the company’s AI roadmap.
claims.quote: Additionally, we have a long‑term strategic partnership with OpenAI.

claims.claim: Microsoft has set 2030 sustainability targets to become carbon negative, water positive and zero waste, and reports progress annually.
claims.quote: In 2020, we announced goals to become a carbon negative, water positive, and zero waste company by 2030.
